headline: Saudi attacks and Hormuz strikes lift Brent to $116.72 as gold slips below $4,000 and yields edge up
summary: More Houthi attacks in Saudi Arabia, tanker strikes near Hormuz and stalled US–Iran diplomacy sent Brent up $3.55 to $116.72, its highest settle since April 29, with December WTI up 3.8% at $103.27 and RBOB up 1.1% to $3.2116. Oil-driven inflation fears and hot PMI price gauges kept a December Fed hike priced near 80%, so gold fell below $4,000 for the first time since July and Treasuries gave back part of Thursday's rally, the 10-year rising about 4bp to near 4.99%. Weak euro-area PMIs held Bunds steady and French yields eased from 24-year highs, and after the close Moody's left France at Aa3.
drivers: Gulf attacks push Brent near its March peak

Houthi strikes across Saudi Arabia forced Aramco to evacuate its Dhahran headquarters, a tanker spill was found off the UAE and Libya cut output after a pipeline valve was shut. Brent settled up 3.1% at $116.72, 6% higher on the week, and WTI rose $3.80 to $103.27 despite a 400,000-barrel SPR loan to Phillips 66.
Prices, not growth, drive Fed pricing

The US flash composite PMI eased to 57.6 as expected, but its prices-charged gauge jumped to 59.8, the highest since August 2022, and Michigan one-year inflation expectations rose to 4.7%. December hike odds held near 80% and October near 9%, lifting the 2-year about 5bp to 4.68%.

Spot gold touched $3,975, its lowest since July, and ended near $3,995, down 0.7% and about 4% on the week, its steepest weekly loss since June. Silver fell about 1.2% to near $53.9 after dipping to $53.

French 10-year yields eased about 3–5bp to near 5.04% and the spread to Bunds narrowed to about 170bp from 177bp as weak PMIs, with France's composite at 48.4 against 50.8 expected, pulled euro yields down. After the close Moody's kept France at Aa3 with a negative outlook, avoiding the downgrade markets had priced.

oil.note: Dec WTI settled up $3.80 (+3.8%) at $103.27; Brent up $3.55 (+3.1%) at $116.72, highest since April 29.
oil.why: Crude extended Thursday's jump as Houthi attacks across Saudi Arabia forced Aramco to evacuate its Dhahran headquarters and October became the worst month yet for attacks on Hormuz shipping. A tanker spill off the UAE, a Libyan pipeline shutdown and Trump saying the US might let the Iran war wind down slowly added risk premium. A 400,000-barrel SPR loan to a Louisiana refinery only briefly checked the rally; Brent gained 6% on the week.
oil.outlook: Bias higher while attacks continue: Brent $110–120 and WTI $98–108. A Brent close above the $118 March high opens new highs for the year; a US–Iran opening or a calm week of Gulf exports would pull it back toward $108.
oil.watch: Saudi and Hormuz attacks, EIA data Oct 28, OPEC+ on Nov 1 and the Nov 3 midterms.

gas.note: Nov RBOB rose 3.51¢ (+1.1%) to $3.2116, a third straight gain but down 0.7% on the week; AAA average about $4.29.
gas.why: Gasoline tracked crude higher for a third day, its best three-day run since late September, and settled at the highest since Oct 16. It lagged crude because the switch to cheaper winter-blend fuel and EIA stocks of 205.3M barrels give it a seasonal cushion, so it was the only NYMEX energy contract down on the week. Diesel rose about 1% to $4.98 and leads the complex.
gas.outlook: Range $3.10–3.35, following crude. Winter blend and softer seasonal demand cap it; a close above $3.30 would need Brent beyond $118, while a crude pullback would send it back to $3.10.
gas.watch: Nov RBOB expiry Oct 30, EIA data Oct 28 and AAA's weekly average.

gold.note: Spot near $3,995, down 0.7% after a $3,975 low, the lowest since July; Dec futures $4,007.90, down 1.3%.
gold.why: Gold slipped below $4,000 for the first time since mid-July as $116 Brent and the hottest PMI selling prices since 2022 reinforced bets on a December Fed hike, priced near 80%. Michigan one-year inflation expectations rising to 4.7% added to the higher-for-longer case, and Treasury yields rose about 4bp. It lost about 4% on the week, the steepest fall since June, with the 5- and 20-day averages still falling.
gold.outlook: Bias lower in a $3,890–4,080 range into the Fed. A close below $3,946 targets $3,890 and then near $3,800; it needs a move back above $4,075 to ease the downtrend.
gold.watch: The Fed on Oct 28, oil and Gulf headlines, and the dollar.

silver.note: Spot near $53.9, down about 1.2% after dipping to $53, its lowest since November 2025; gold/silver ratio near 74.
silver.why: Silver extended Thursday's near-6% slide as oil-driven rate-hike bets and growth worries hit industrial metals, with platinum and palladium also at multi-month lows. Equities fell again and investors kept cutting precious-metal positions after the tech-led liquidation, keeping silver below the $54.50 resistance Kitco flagged. Its relative weakness left the gold/silver ratio near 74.
silver.outlook: Bias lower in a $51.40–55.80 range. A break below $52.40 opens $51.40 and, per CPM, possibly $50; it needs a close above $55.80 to stabilise.
silver.watch: The Fed on Oct 28, equity sentiment, copper and China data.

us2y.note: Up about 5bp to near 4.68%, after Thursday's 19bp drop; still a fourth weekly decline.
us2y.why: The 2-year gave back part of Thursday's plunge as the flight to safety faded and tech shares steadied. The flash PMI's prices-charged index rose to 59.8, the highest since August 2022, and Michigan one-year inflation expectations climbed to 4.7%, keeping December hike odds near 80% even as October odds held near 9%. Brent's rise to $116.72 added to the inflation worry.
us2y.outlook: Range 4.60–4.80% until the Fed. A clear signal for a December hike would lift it toward 4.75–4.80%; renewed equity stress or a cautious statement would retest 4.60%.
us2y.watch: The Fed on Oct 27–28, 2-year auction next week and October jobs data.

us5y.note: About 4.81%, up roughly 4bp; the belly gave back part of Thursday's rally.
us5y.why: The 5-year rose with the front end as hot price gauges in the flash PMI and $103 WTI revived inflation risk and the haven bid eased with tech stocks steadier. Composite activity of 57.6, in line with forecasts and still near a five-year high, shows little need for the Fed to back away from a December hike.
us5y.outlook: Range 4.72–4.95%. Oil above $110 keeps the risk tilted higher; a hawkish Fed would push it back toward 4.90%, while a renewed equity slide would retest 4.72%.
us5y.watch: The Fed on Oct 28, the 5-year auction next week and oil.

us10y.note: Up about 4bp to near 4.99%, briefly above 5% before New York; down about 8–11bp on the week.
us10y.why: The 10-year retraced part of Thursday's 19bp fall, its biggest since March 2023, as tech stocks steadied and Brent jumped 3%. The PMI showed selling prices rising at the fastest pace since 2022, and Michigan long-run inflation expectations rose to 3.5%. Lingering doubts about debt-funded AI spending and French stress kept it just below 5%, and the curve flattened as the 2-year rose more.
us10y.outlook: Range 4.90–5.10%. Oil above $100, heavy supply and a December hike limit the downside; a hawkish Fed would likely put it back above 5%, while a new equity selloff would test 4.90%.
us10y.watch: The Fed on Oct 28, oil, the Nov 3 midterms and the Nov 4 refunding.

us30y.note: Up about 3–4bp to near 5.32%, lagging the front end as the curve flattened.
us30y.why: The long bond rose less than shorter notes as markets added to December hike bets rather than to term premium, flattening the curve. Some haven demand remained after the AI-led selloff, but higher oil and supply worries ahead of the midterms and the Nov 4 refunding kept investors cautious about the longest maturities.
us30y.outlook: Range 5.22–5.42%. The refunding sets the next leg: smaller long-bond sizes would help it rally, unchanged sizes and $115-plus oil would push it back toward 5.40%.
us30y.watch: The Fed on Oct 28, the midterms Nov 3 and the Nov 4 refunding.

de2y.note: Near 3.03%, roughly flat after Thursday's rally.
de2y.why: The Schatz held steady as weak flash PMIs offset Brent's jump. The euro-area composite fell to 51.9 from 53.1, below every Reuters forecast and a four-month low, while input costs rose sharply again on energy. Economists expect the ECB to hold its 2.50% deposit rate next week and hike in December, so the mix of slowing growth and rising costs left front-end pricing little changed.
de2y.outlook: Range 2.95–3.12%. A hawkish ECB on Oct 29 would lift it toward 3.10%; further weak data or a drop in oil would test 2.95%.
de2y.watch: The ECB on Oct 29 and flash October inflation.

de5y.note: About 3.14%, little changed while US yields rose.
de5y.why: The 5-year Bund held steady as weaker PMIs in Germany (52.8 against 53.3 expected), France and the euro area outweighed higher oil. Haven demand eased a little from Thursday as French yields fell back, but rising input prices kept investors from pricing a shorter ECB tightening cycle.
de5y.outlook: Range 3.05–3.22%. French spread tightening after Moody's would take away some haven demand; a hawkish ECB would lift it toward the top of the range.
de5y.watch: Monday's reaction to Moody's, the ECB on Oct 29 and the OAT–Bund spread.

de10y.note: Near 3.33–3.35%, roughly flat (Dow Jones: down 1bp to 3.330%); OAT–Bund spread about 170bp.
de10y.why: The 10-year Bund barely moved as soft euro-area PMIs balanced Brent's rise to $116.72 and the rise in Treasury yields. The weak French PMI showed confidence at its lowest since April 2020, keeping demand for German debt firm. With French yields falling, the spread narrowed from Thursday's 15-year high of 177bp.
de10y.outlook: Range 3.25–3.45%. Moody's holding France could ease the haven bid and nudge it up; a move above 3.45% would need a hawkish ECB or a strong equity recovery.
de10y.watch: Monday's French reaction, the ECB on Oct 29 and euro inflation data.

de30y.note: About 3.70%, up about 1bp, tracking a firmer US long end.
de30y.why: The 30-year Bund edged higher with US long bonds as oil climbed, while weak PMIs limited the rise. It follows global term premium more than ECB pricing, so the 3bp rise in the US 30-year mattered more than the euro-area data. Supply worries at the long end also limited any haven buying.
de30y.outlook: Range 3.60–3.80%. It follows US long bonds and global supply more than the ECB.
de30y.watch: US long-end yields, the Nov 4 refunding and German long-dated sales.

fr2y.note: About 3.79%, a little higher; the gap to the Schatz holds near 75bp.
fr2y.why: Short French debt lagged the rest of the curve as political risk stayed in front-end pricing. The French composite PMI fell to 48.4, well below the 50.8 forecast, and business confidence turned negative for the first time in nearly two years, with firms citing next year's election and public finances. That points to slower growth that makes the deficit target harder to hit.
fr2y.outlook: Range 3.70–3.85%. Moody's hold should keep it calm; it would jump only if the budget collapsed or a censure motion threatened the government.
fr2y.watch: Monday's reaction to Moody's, the budget debate from Oct 27 and the ECB on Oct 29.

fr5y.note: About 4.43%, roughly flat; the spread to Germany held near its widest.
fr5y.why: The 5-year OAT steadied after a week of heavy selling as investors squared positions before Moody's review, which most analysts expected to bring a downgrade. Danske Bank called a cut fully priced, so the risk was in the outlook. The weak French PMI helped yields fall, offset by worries over a deficit above 5% of GDP.
fr5y.outlook: Bias lower in a 4.30–4.50% range after Moody's held Aa3. A budget setback in parliament would push it back toward 4.50%.
fr5y.watch: Monday's open, the budget debate from Oct 27 and the ECB on Oct 29.

fr10y.note: Eased about 3–5bp to near 5.04% from Thursday's 5.142% high; spread to Bunds about 170bp.
fr10y.why: French 10-year yields fell back from 24-year highs as the weak October PMI, at 48.4, pulled euro-area yields lower and the spread to Bunds narrowed from 177bp to about 170bp. Yields still rose nearly 27bp on the week, the most since May. After the close Moody's kept France at Aa3 with a negative outlook, avoiding the downgrade most had expected.
fr10y.outlook: Spread bias narrower toward 160–165bp after Moody's held, in a 160–185bp range. A failed budget vote or fresh unrest would put 177bp back in play.
fr10y.watch: Monday's reaction to Moody's, the budget debate from Oct 27 and the ECB on Oct 29.

fr30y.note: About 5.49%, down about 1bp, still near cycle highs.
fr30y.why: The 30-year OAT edged lower with the rest of the curve but stayed close to its highs as investors still demand a large premium to hold long French debt through the budget fight and the 2027 presidential race. The weak PMI eased yields a little, but debt-service costs and political risk weigh most at the long end.
fr30y.outlook: Bias for modest relief after Moody's, range 5.35–5.60%. A close above 5.60% would set a new high; a credible budget deal is what would turn it.
fr30y.watch: Moody's reaction Monday, the budget debate and long-dated OAT auctions.

watch: Next: Monday's reaction to Moody's hold on France, the French budget debate from Oct 27, the Fed on Oct 28, EIA data Oct 28, the ECB on Oct 29, Nov RBOB expiry Oct 30, OPEC+ on Nov 1, the US midterms Nov 3 and the Nov 4 refunding.
